SMTO-EXE-0096 — Reading the text took too long or produced too much

GUID: 044299eb-fa2c-52f8-a2d1-2ac506272a3e
Slug: screen-ocr-limit
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO gives text reading a short time limit (about ten seconds for screen text) and a size limit. This screen or image had too much to read, so SMTO stopped. No text was returned.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to read one window or part of the screen instead of the whole display. A smaller area has less text, so it finishes within the time limit.
  2. If you gave SMTO an image file, crop it to just the part with the text you need, then ask again. Cropping removes text you don't need, which keeps the result under the size limit.
  3. For a long page or document, ask SMTO to read it in several smaller pieces. Each piece gets its own time and size allowance.

What success looks like

  • SMTO returns the text from the smaller area or image.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it, with roughly how large the area or image was, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the screen contents into the report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Local Tesseract OCR hit its subprocess deadline or output cap (10 seconds and 2 MiB TSV for screen text recognition; 20 seconds and 32 MiB for searchable PDF) and was stopped.

What this means

  • Local OCR reached its subprocess deadline or output-size bound. Screen text recognition uses a ten-second/2 MiB TSV bound; searchable PDF generation has its separate bounded path. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Local OCR reached its subprocess deadline or output-size bound. Screen text recognition uses a ten-second/2 MiB TSV bound; searchable PDF generation has its separate bounded path.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the OCR operation type, selected region, language and applicable time/output bound.

How to fix it

  • Tesseract.recognize ran past its 10-second deadline or 2 MiB raw TSV cap (searchable PDF uses a separate 20-second/32 MiB limit); the worker process was killed and reaped. Make a new explicit OCR request on a smaller region or image.
  • Choose a smaller screen region or image and make a new explicit request. OCR has a ten-second processing budget and a 2 MiB raw TSV bound.

Retry and execution caution

  • Choose a smaller screen region or image and make a new explicit request. OCR has a ten-second processing budget and a 2 MiB raw TSV bound.

How to verify the fix

  • A smaller or otherwise valid explicit OCR request completes within its own bounds without losing required content.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
